title: Restore replaces the current career even when every choice says Keep current
steps: Save a backup of Daniel and Nik's three-season Showdown after season 1 (11–11).
Have a different ten-season Showdown with nine seasons saved (99–99).
Open Settings, then OPEN HISTORY & BACKUP. Choose the earlier backup and press REVIEW RESTORE.
Choose Keep current active state, Keep current Legacy only, Keep current preferences, and Keep current Save Library.
Check the ready plan: it promises the current career stays and no changes are needed.
Press APPLY RESTORE and accept the game's confirmation.
Export another backup or reload and reopen the game: the current career is now the earlier one-season career.
expected: The current ten-season Showdown keeps all nine saved seasons and its 99–99 total. Its current career selection, completed history and preferences all stay as chosen.
actual: The current nine-season career is replaced by the backup career with one saved season and an 11–11 total. The game announces a successful restore. Completed history and preferences remain unchanged. The replacement survives reload.
root_cause: The preview includes the current collection of careers. Apply builds its plan at restore.js:283 using currentRaw, which omits that collection. Normal current games also have no old single-career entry, so createCareerModeRestorePlan wrongly calls the destination empty and restores the entire backup collection despite Keep current. The later complete-state checks verify the write but do not compare the applied plan with the previewed promise.

fix.change: Build the apply plan from completeRaw when the complete current-career snapshot is available, matching the preview. Require an explicit replace choice before replacing an existing collection of careers. Check both a populated and an empty backup while Keep current is selected.
